Il carcinoma a cellule chiare è il tumor:
Clear cell carcinoma is the most common malignant renal tumour in adults (about 70-75%). The cells have clear cytoplasm (lipid and glycogen) or, in high-grade areas, eosinophilic cytoplasm; they are arranged in nests and alveoli surrounded by a rich capillary network. The grade (ISUP/WHO) is based on the nucleoli; grade 4 includes marked atypia and sarcomatoid or rhabdoid features.
Radiological correlation (case 088, CT of the same patient): the capillary network explains the intense, early enhancement with washout; necrosis and haemorrhage make it heterogeneous; intracytoplasmic fat may cause signal drop on opposed-phase MRI. High grade and size go with haematogenous metastases: here multiple lung metastases (M1).
Carcinoma a cellule chiare: nidi di cell: Clear cell carcinoma: nests of clear cells in a dense capillary network, i.e. hypervascular on CT and MRI.
